important.name: B10 dropped on a baseline the plan-1014 fixture contaminated
important.summary:
The scenario fixture plan-1014 is a byte-identical copy of the live plan 1014 (same blobs as docs/plans/1014_strap_reopen_ActionPlan.json and its PIP). Its STR-1 action (fixture ActionPlan line 218, PIP line 132) spells out the exact rules round 2 tests: '(a) a lane that needs a file outside its item stops and reports instead of building past the plan ... (c) a frozen receipts plan's JSON and HTML page are never edited by hand'. The B10 baseline task (SC-4) has the runner write a lane prompt from that plan, and the recorded baseline R-2 echoes the plan text almost verbatim ('stop and report which file and why; do not build past the plan', 'its JSON and HTML page are never hand-edited'), although the write-plan SKILL.md at the round-2 base b7c6209 has no stop-and-report rule (no match for stop/report/build past). B10 was then dropped (SkillSpec.json:572) because 'the drawn baseline already told the lane to stop and report ... under the pre-receipts SKILL.md'. The baseline passed on the fixture's text, not on the old SKILL.md, so the drop reason is false and the lane deviation stop added in plan 1013 stays unproven. This contradicts the strap-skills premise that a run must not carry instructions the agent would not see in real use (strap-skills SKILL.md:14-16). B9 is unaffected in direction: its baseline R-1 failed despite the same leak, so its baseline/green difference is still attributable to the SKILL.md.

Also (roast): Plan 1014 STR-1 asks for three judgment behaviors: (a) a lane stops and reports a deviation, (b) a mid-build change goes through `evolution_api.add` with `--also/--substitute --cite`, and (c) a frozen receipts plan's JSON and HTML page are never hand-edited. The round 2 spec has B9, which covers (b), and B10, which covers (a) and is dropped with a reason. No behavior covers (c). B9's `file_unchanged` check guards only the plan JSON, not `1014_strap_reopen_PIP.html`, and baseline R-1 did rewrite that page. The DesignEvolution has EX1 for the fixture files only. Nothing records that (c) was folded into B9 or left out, yet receipts/STR-1.json says `complete`. The frozen plan and its receipt now disagree about what was proven.
fix: Build a separate frozen receipts fixture plan whose item text does not state the rules under test (for example a plan without the STR-1 item, frozen through plan.py), point B9/B10-style scenarios at it, then `strap.py reopen write-plan --base b7c6209...` for round 3 and add the lane-stop behavior again with that fixture, as step 9 of strap-skills advises for a behavior that still matters.

At minimum, record the contamination: add a DesignEvolution entry for STR-1 stating that B10's drop rests on a baseline that read the rule from the fixture, so the dropped_reason is not taken as evidence that the old SKILL.md taught it.
Record the scope change with `evolution_api.add` (EX2, items STR-1): (c) is covered by B9's `file_unchanged` check on the plan JSON, and the PIP page is not covered. Then re-record STR-1 citing EX2.
Or reopen write-plan for a round 3 with a behavior for (c) whose checks include `file_unchanged` on the PIP html.

important.name: Recorded baseline R-1 shows a scenario runner writing to the main checkout's frozen plan
important.summary:
The R-1 reply stored in the write-plan spec says the runner's first `plan_api.write` and `plan.py freeze 1014 --refreeze` ran with cwd in the main checkout, because `plan.py` takes its project from cwd. It then restored `docs/plans/1014_strap_reopen_ActionPlan.json` and the PIP with `git show HEAD:<path>` and warned that the line endings may have changed. This breaks the runner contract in plugins/harness/agents/strap-scenario-runner.md:39-41 ('Never touch the repository the row names with --repo, any other checkout'). The new plan-1014 fixture makes the leak likely: its DOC-1 and STR-1 commands (fixture ActionPlan.json lines 196, 232 and 236) hard-code `E:/automation/operator-straps/...`, which is the real checkout, so a runner that follows the plan text drives the live repository. Here the frozen plan only survived because the runner noticed and reverted. A run that does not notice breaks the real plan's freeze digest or writes receipts into it, and the recorded evidence still looks clean, because the checks only read TREE.

Also (overall): The R-1 reply stored in the write-plan spec says the runner's first `plan_api.write` and `freeze --refreeze` ran with cwd in the main checkout, because `plan.py` takes its project from cwd. It then restored the plan JSON and PIP with `git show HEAD:<path>`, possibly with changed line endings. The runner contract (`strap-scenario-runner.md:40`) forbids touching the repository the row names. Nothing tells the runner that `plan.py` and `strap.py` need `--repo <TREE>`, so plan-driver scenarios such as B9 can leak into the developer's checkout again.
fix: Make the run brief that `strap.py init` prints (and the strap-scenario-runner rule at strap-scenario-runner.md:39-41) require `--repo "<TREE>"` on every project driver call (`plan.py`, `strap.py`, `harness-skill-api`). Have it state that drivers resolve the project from cwd, which starts in the real checkout.

Have `strap.py run`/`init` refuse or flag a run whose main checkout `git status --porcelain` changed between `init` and `record-run`, so a leak becomes a `problem:` line rather than a confession in the reply.

Add to the runner agent's rules: project drivers (`plan.py`, `strap.py`) inside a scenario run with `--repo <TREE>`. Confirm the main checkout's `docs/plans/1014_strap_reopen_*` files match HEAD byte for byte.

important.name: red skip of green behaviors lets a reopened behavior's new tests bypass the red gate
important.summary:
_red_plan now skips every mechanical behavior in state green, on the claim that green means 'frozen in an earlier round'. Before reopen a green behavior only existed on a frozen spec, where update_behavior is refused. After cmd_reopen clears frozen, strap_api.update_behavior (strap_api.py:211-220) can replace the tests of a green mechanical behavior: mechanical behaviors are never drawn, so _refuse_fields does not lock them, and the state stays green. red then skips the new planned tests, and _mechanical_gate (strap.py:862-867) accepts state green, so freeze passes tests that were never shown to fail first. The red-before-green contract is bypassed for any behavior carried over from an earlier round.

Also (roast): `_red_plan` now skips every mechanical behavior in state `green`, using the state as a stand-in for 'frozen in an earlier round, tests already proven red'. After `reopen` the spec is unfrozen, so `strap_api.update_behavior(name, "B1", tests=[...])` is accepted: mechanical behaviors are never drawn, so `_LOCKED_WHEN_DRAWN` does not lock their `tests`, and the state stays `green`. `red` then skips the new nodes, and `_mechanical_gate` accepts state GREEN plus passing tests, so a test written after its code freezes without ever failing. That breaks the Iron Law in strap-skills SKILL.md lines 53-56 ('a mechanical one only when its planned tests failed red as planned'). Before this PR the hole could not open: a mechanical behavior became green only at freeze, and a frozen spec refused `update_behavior`. The state flag says 'was green once', not 'these exact tests were proven red', and the gate trusts it for both.

Also (overall): `_red_plan` skips every mechanical behavior in state `green`, assuming its planned tests are the ones proven red in an earlier round. After `reopen` the spec is unfrozen, so `strap_api.update_behavior(name, 'B1', tests=[...])` is accepted (mechanical behaviors are never drawn, so `_LOCKED_WHEN_DRAWN` does not lock them) and the state stays `green`. `red` then skips the new nodes, and `_mechanical_gate` accepts `green` plus passing tests. Result: new planned tests reach a frozen spec without ever failing first. Before this PR a frozen spec refused every behavior edit, so reopen opens this path. Round 1 has a similar gap for a behavior edited after `red` (state `red`), but there the code usually does not exist yet. Here it already exists at the new base, so the tests pass unproven.
fix: In strap_api.update_behavior, reset a behavior's state to open when a change touches tests (or statement) of a behavior in state green, so red runs its planned tests again.
Or have _red_plan skip only the behaviors listed in spec.rounds[-1].behaviors whose tests are unchanged since that round (store a digest of each behavior's tests in Round), and run red for the rest.

In `strap_api._refuse_fields`, refuse `tests` and `kind` on any behavior id listed in `spec.rounds[*].behaviors` (an earlier round's mechanical proof stays as it was proven). A changed test then goes on a new behavior, and that behavior runs red.

Alternatively, skip red in `_red_plan` only when the behavior's planned tests equal the ones frozen in the last round: store a per-behavior tests digest in `Round` at reopen and compare against it. A behavior whose tests changed drops back into the red plan, and `_mechanical_gate` requires a fresh RED for it.
Add a test to tests/scripts/test_strap_reopen.py: reopen, `update_behavior` B1 with a new node whose file already passes, then assert that `red` covers B1 or that the update is refused.
In `strap_api.update_behavior`, when `tests` (or `kind`) is in the changes and the behavior is in state `green` or `red`, reset its state to `open` so `red` picks it up again.
Or refuse `tests` changes on a behavior listed in any `rounds[*].behaviors`; a changed rule then becomes a new behavior.

important.name: reopen does not ensure the new base holds the frozen round's parts
important.summary: The _red_plan docstring (strap.py:405) states that a green behavior's code 'exists at the new base', and the module docstring says base moves to HEAD. cmd_reopen (strap.py:907-919) takes HEAD or any ancestor REF through _edit_base without checking that the frozen parts are committed there. When the frozen round is still uncommitted (freeze runs on the working tree, the developer commits later) or --base names a commit older than the previous round's base, the new base lacks the round's code and SKILL.md text: red for new behaviors runs on a tree without the modules they build on (an ImportError instead of the planned exception, or a planned ImportError met for the wrong reason), and baseline runs of new judgment behaviors read a SKILL.md from before the earlier round (_skill_text, strap.py:637-640). _edit_base also checks SKILL.md only at HEAD, not at REF.
fix: In cmd_reopen, refuse when any part path differs between the chosen base and the working tree (`git diff --quiet <base> -- <parts>` plus a check for untracked part files), with a problem line telling the author to commit the frozen round first.
Also refuse a --base that is not a descendant of the previous spec.base (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <spec.base> <base>`) when spec.base is set.

minor.name: Reopen's base rule covers baselines but not red, and omits that the base is fixed for the round
minor.summary:
SKILL.md:249-250 says to pick the base by one rule: the commit whose code the new scenarios need but whose SKILL.md lacks the new guidance. `red` also runs at that base (strap.py:388-390 `_start_commit`, used at strap.py:419). So a round that adds a mechanical behavior needs a base where that behavior's code does not exist yet; otherwise its planned nodes pass at red and `red` refuses. Once a round is open, its base cannot change. `reopen` refuses a spec that is not frozen (strap.py:910-911), `new --edit --base` on an existing spec only resumes it, and the API sets no `base`. A wrong pick therefore lasts until the next freeze. The paragraph also drops the condition step 1 states and the driver enforces: `--base` must be an ancestor of HEAD (strap.py:274-275).

Also (skill_package): SKILL.md:251-252 says 'The earlier behaviors are gated again at the next freeze', then explains only the mechanical case. Writing the new guidance changes SKILL.md and with it the content hash. `_judgment_gate` (strap.py:843-849) then needs a passing green on the current hash for every earlier judgment behavior, not only the new ones. `draw` skips behaviors already drawn (strap.py:447-449), so 'continue from step 2 for the new behaviors' never prompts green runs for the earlier ones. The session finds out only at the freeze, from `no passing green on the current hash` lines. The refreeze paragraph at SKILL.md:225-229 does state this rule for a part change; the reopen paragraph does not.

Also (overall): The SKILL.md paragraph says only that earlier behaviors are 'gated again', and spells out just the mechanical case (skips red, planned tests rerun). `_judgment_gate` requires a passing green on the current hash for every live judgment behavior, earlier rounds included. So once a round-2 SKILL.md edit changes the hash, every round-1 judgment behavior needs `run --arm green` and grades again before `freeze` passes. The paragraph also does not say that the first `freeze` after a reopen prints `| was <hash12>`; line 236 says that only for `--refreeze`. The write-plan round 2 in this PR never hit the judgment case, because round 1 had no draws or runs and the hash did not change.
fix: After 'since baselines read the SKILL.md at `base`.' add: '`red` also runs at `base`, so a new mechanical behavior's code must not exist there yet. `--base` must be an ancestor of HEAD, and the base stays fixed until the next freeze.'
After 'and its planned tests rerun.' add: 'An earlier judgment behavior keeps its baselines but needs a passing green on the new hash: run and grade its greens as in step 10.'

Extend the paragraph: 'a judgment one needs a passing green on the new hash once a part changes (run and grade it as in step 10); the first freeze after a reopen prints `| was <hash12>` from the last round.'

minor.name: Tautological `assert sm.Round is not None` guards
minor.summary:
`assert sm.Round is not None` (lines 49 and 57) can never fail on its own terms: a missing `Round` raises AttributeError before the comparison, and a present class is never None. At line 49 it is redundant, because lines 51-53 already fail without the `rounds` field. At line 57 it is the only line that makes the backward-compatibility test fail before the change, so it acts as a hidden red-phase guard that looks like a no-op.

Also (tests): The module docstring (lines 3-5) says a pre-`rounds` spec must dump and digest byte for byte as before. `_old_driver_digest` rebuilds the old digest from the new `sm.dump_spec` output, so it pins the driver-digest key set but not the dump text. The dump check only asserts that `rounds` is absent (line 59), and `authored_digest` is never compared for the empty-rounds case.
fix: Delete line 49; replace line 57 with `assert "rounds" in sm.SkillSpec.model_fields`, which states what the guard protects.
Keep line 57 and add a one-line comment saying it makes the test fail on a model without `Round`.
Pin literal values computed at the merge base for `_spec()`: the exact `dump_spec` text and the `driver_digest` and `authored_digest` hex strings. Assert equality against them.
Narrow the module docstring to what is checked: `rounds` stays out of the dump and the driver digest.

minor.summary:

Three branches of `cmd_reopen` and `cmd_freeze` are untested: (1) a dropped behavior is left out of `Round.behaviors` (strap.py:913); (2) an edit-mode spec keeps its previous non-None `base` in the round (strap.py:914); (3) a second reopen appends round 3, and the next freeze names `rounds[-1]` (strap.py:890, 918).

Also (overall): `test_strap_reopen.py` covers HEAD as base and a ref that names no commit. It does not cover a valid ancestor `--base` (the path STR-1 actually used: `spec.base` set to that SHA and printed as `base <sha12>`), the 'not an ancestor of HEAD' refusal, a second reopen (round 3, two `rounds` entries), or a judgment behavior from an earlier round being refused at freeze until it gets a green on the new hash.

Also (roast): test_strap_reopen.py tests only the default base and the 'names no commit' refusal. Three paths have no test: `--base <ancestor>` landing in `base`, the 'is not an ancestor of HEAD' refusal, and a second reopen (round 3: `rounds` appended rather than replaced, `round 3` printed, and freeze's `was` read from `rounds[-1]`). The design's headline goal ('the next freeze gates every live behavior, earlier ones included') is shown for a mechanical behavior only. No test checks that a round-1 judgment behavior blocks the freeze with 'no passing green on the current hash' once a part changes after reopen. The happy path is covered; the paths most likely to regress are not.
fix: Add a test that drops a behavior, freezes, reopens twice, and asserts: `rounds[0].behaviors` omits the dropped id, `rounds[1].base` equals the first reopen's base, the output says 'round 3', and the next freeze's 'was' names `rounds[-1]`.

Add a test that commits twice, reopens with `--base HEAD~1` and asserts `spec['base']` and the printed sha12; add the not-an-ancestor refusal; add a freeze-reopen-freeze-reopen test asserting `round 3` and `len(rounds) == 2`.

Add tests to tests/scripts/test_strap_reopen.py: reopen with `--base HEAD~1` (commit twice in the fixture) and assert `spec['base']` is that sha; reopen with a non-ancestor ref and assert the refusal; freeze, reopen, freeze, reopen, and assert two rounds plus `round 3` in the output.
Add a judgment-behavior variant: freeze a spec holding one judgment behavior, reopen, edit SKILL.md, and assert that freeze refuses with `B1: no passing green on the current hash`.

fix: Track fence state while scanning the lines and require the launch line to fall between ``` markers.
Drop 'in a fence' from the docstring and 'fenced' from the assertion message.
Slice the body from `**Reopen for new behaviors.**` to `13. **Hand off.**` and assert `--base` and `rounds` inside that slice.
